messages:
maya: Heads-up — we need a compact set of continuous-batching signals on the console before next sprint kickoff. Goal: identify saturation early and surface routing-policy impact per-route/model. Looking for runtime + infra inputs and a rough owner timeline.

alex: Can you list the must-have signals? I can prototype panels if we have concrete metric names and labels.

jun: From runtime side I can emit these out-of-the-box: per-shard batch_size_hist (buckets), runtime_queue_depth (gauge), wait_seconds histogram (for p50/p95/p99), and prefill_saturation_ratio (gauge 0..1). We can add labels: shard, model, route, tier, customer_hash.

maya: Solid. Important: console needs aggregated, low-cardinality views by default. Product wants per-route visibility; engineering wants per-shard for debugging. We should avoid exposing raw customer hashes in dashboards.

olivia: UX ask: create a single "Saturation" summary metric that combines queue_depth/instance_capacity + wait_p95 + fraction_of_small_batches. That makes it easier for product folks to scan. Panel drilldowns can show decomposition.

samir: SRE perspective: we need clear alerting thresholds. Proposal: p95_wait > 200ms sustained for 2m -> warning; queue_depth > 80% capacity for 5m -> critical. Also alert on sudden drop in batch_size median (possible head-of-line starvation).

alex: Proposed PromQL examples to standardize (we can tweak):

```promql
# batch composition (histogram rates per shard, route)
sum by (shard, route, model) (rate(runtime_batch_size_bucket[1m]))

# queue depth averaged per shard
avg by (shard) (runtime_queue_depth)

# p95 wait time for route
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(runtime_wait_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route, shard))
```

jun: Labels we plan: shard, model, route, tier. customer_hash will be emitted but we should only use it for rollups/topk off-line; don't include in default dashboards to avoid cardinality blowups. We can also emit synthesized labels like routing_policy to capture fallback vs primary.

leo: I'll own the Grafana panel templates and console wiring. For panels I need sample queries and a small sample event stream (so we can demo the heatmap / composition). @jun can you paste a tiny sample payload?

jun: Sample compact lines (runtime will emit protobuf/json; here is a toy example):

```json
{"ts": 1678890000, "shard": "s1", "route": "text-gen", "model": "gpt-xxxx", "batch_sizes": {"1":10,"2":40,"4":120}, "queue_depth": 12, "wait_ms_p95": 85}
{"ts": 1678890060, "shard": "s1", "route": "text-gen", "model": "gpt-xxxx", "batch_sizes": {"1":5,"2":30,"4":150}, "queue_depth": 18, "wait_ms_p95": 210}
```

olivia: Perfect. For console UX: panels to include — Top routes by saturation (sorted), Batch composition heatmap (batch size buckets over time), Wait time timeseries (p50/p95/p99), Queue depth per-shard map. Drilldowns should show recent sample traces/logs and the routing_policy label.

sre-bot: incident-bot: deploy to runtime cluster/canary completed (build id: b-2026-03-18-09).

samir: On exposing to customers: product asked for read-only per-route percentiles. Security: allow read-only per-route aggregated metrics but never per-customer. Audit on who queried what. Also roll this into the metrics privacy doc.

maya: Timeline proposal: Jun emits metrics by EOD Wednesday, Alex drafts dashboard prototype Thursday, Leo wires panels into the console Friday, SRE reviews alert thresholds Monday. Owners: @jun for metrics, @alex for dashboard queries, @leo for console integration, @samir for alerts/security.

alex: I'll open a short RFC for the metric naming and tags (so consumers can rely on stable names). Also will add entries to the metric-catalog repo explaining cardinality guidance.

jun: Will add metric metadata tags (e.g., redwood.metric=continuous_batching) and include typical cardinality notes.

maya: Great — I'll follow up with a tiny checklist in the #eng-platform tracker. If anyone sees missing signals (e.g., prefill latency, eviction count), flag here.

leo: One more note — for capacity calculations we should surface instance GPU memory and in-flight token budget per-shard. That will help compute true saturation rather than pure queue depth. I can add that to the dashboard requirements.

maya: Noted. Thanks everyone — will ping later with PR links. :thumbsup:
